subject: physics

items.q: Can thermal radiation travel through empty space?
items.correct: Yes — it is infrared electromagnetic waves and needs no medium, like the Sun's heat reaching Earth.
items.misconception: No, heat radiation cannot cross a vacuum because there are no particles.
items.random_wrong: Radiation can only travel through metals.
items.why: Thermal radiation is EM waves, so it needs no particles. That is exactly how energy from the Sun reaches us across empty space.

items.q: How are power and energy different?
items.correct: Power is the rate of energy transfer (watts, J/s); energy is the total amount transferred (joules).
items.misconception: Power and energy are the same thing and share the same unit.
items.random_wrong: Power is energy multiplied by time.
items.why: Power = energy ÷ time. A higher-power device transfers energy faster; the energy transferred = power × time.

items.q: What does the width of an arrow on a Sankey diagram represent?
items.correct: The amount of energy transferred along that path — wider means more energy.
items.misconception: Every arrow is drawn the same width.
items.random_wrong: The width shows the speed of the energy, not the amount.
items.why: Sankey diagrams show energy flow; arrow thickness is proportional to energy, so wasted-energy branches make the useful-output arrow narrower.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Energy Resources & Energy Transfers
